parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
I've had a look at your draft presentation plan and compared it with mine, Cath. And we seem to have the same basic structure. We've both included the same three main sections, that's the anatomy of the foot, the injuries and the treatment.

And we've organised our presentations in the same way,but the types of sports we've chosen to illustrate the possible injuries aren't the same.

I'll deal with the anatomy bit. I've got notes and a handout on that from Professor Gilligan's lecture.

Oh, I was hoping to do that. I've downloaded some useful stuff. I do think we should limit this section though. We don't want to spend much time on anatomy when the main focus is on the treatment.

That's true, but in the last section maybe the two of us could show how some of therapies actually work. I could be the patient and you could do the treatment.

Good idea, because it's hard to find pictures as injuries are mostly internal. It would be good to hear some first-hand accounts from injured athletes too.

Yeah, but we don't have time.

No, should we then discuss different types of heel injury? It's worth pointing out that these vary enormously in how bad they are. It might be just a pulled muscle or a bone injury which needs surgery. Sometimes only an expert can tell the difference.

Excellent. I'll do the slides on that. Leave that one to me.

Now, what about causes of heel injuries?

Well, it's easy enough to list them: over-use, improper footwear.

Yes, incorrect running style.

They're all relevant, but for simplicity let's just pick one cause. Say, stuff about changing your training habit suddenly.

You mean like suddenly doing a lot of mountain training? Yes, that's a good idea. And there was research on that in the latest edition of Physio Journal, wasn't there? Professor Gilligan recommended it to us.

Great. You can leave the bit on stretching techniques to me. I really like that stuff.

So, what's going to be your approach there?

Well, I'll summarise all the various techniques with visual support. And then, I'll make the point that the stretching should be carefully managed. Obviously, you have to be careful not to over-stretch and to stretch only when your muscles are warmed up. Otherwise, you could do yourself more harm than good. It's also important that on a supervised programme stretching is later on combined with balance exercises, which stretch and also strengthen the muscles.

Okay, then.

It's always useful to have some information on case studies at the end, in case we're short of material. Did you manage to find anything?

Yes, a female runner in her 30s talking about her treatment for a swollen heel. Initially, she rested the injury. This did help to reduce the swelling, although it was still a little bit uncomfortable. Then, she applied an ice pack to the injury twice a day.

Did that work?

Well, she persisted with this treatment for the first month, but decided it wasn't helping. After this period, she was shown how to use deep tissue massage techniques, and was surprised at how much freedom of movement this created in her foot.

Wasn't she having ultrasound treatment?

Yes, she was having sessions at the hospital, but she remained unconvinced about its value, as she felt the same about the balancing exercises she was prescribed.

Okay, that's interesting. I looked at the Aftercare programme of a male sprinter, who was allowed to do some sports activity as part of his rehabilitation. After four months of treatment, he did some light running on grass, wearing shoes that gave plenty of support to his injured heel.

So, it didn't hurt?

Well, he found the heel was sore afterwards, and the same happened with some jumping exercises he was asked to try.

Did he go to the gym and use weights?

Yes, after a few weeks. And if he used light weights, he could train without pain. He also tried cycling, and found this beneficial, as his foot was not making contact with the ground. He expected a similar result with swimming, but found the repetitive kicking motion was actually aggravating the injury.

Well, both these case studies have value.

questions.question: John and Cath's presentation plans are different in

analyses.content: John 提到虽然结构和顺序一样，但他们用来“说明”（illustrate）可能受伤情况的运动类型（types of sports）是不同的，这对应选项中的 examples。
And we've organised our presentations in the same way, but the types of sports we've chosen to illustrate the possible injuries aren't the same.
不要选 B 或 C，录音开头明确说了 "same basic structure" 和 "organised... in the same way"，说明结构和要点安排是一样的。

options.optionContent: It would be better if Cath spoke about it.

options.optionContent: It should be kept quite short.

options.optionContent: It should be based on information from the internet.

questions.question: What do the students agree about the anatomy section of their presentation?

analyses.content: I do think we should limit this section though. We don't want to spend much time on anatomy...
不要因为听到 "downloaded" 或 "notes" 就选 A 或 C，重点在于两人最终达成的一致意见是“篇幅要短”。
Cath 认为应该限制（limit）解剖学这部分的内容，不要花太多时间，John 表示同意（That's true）。

questions.question: What do the students agree to include in the last section?

analyses.content: ...maybe the two of us could show how some of therapies actually work. I could be the patient and you could do the treatment.
不要选 A（图片），因为 John 说很难找到内部损伤的图片；也不要选 C（采访），Cath 说没有时间（don't have time）。
两人商定在最后一部分通过角色扮演（be the patient... do the treatment）来展示治疗方法，即“演示”。

options.option: Some are more serious than others.
options.optionContent: Some are more serious than others.

questions.question: What is said about the different types of heel injury?

analyses.content: It's worth pointing out that these vary enormously in how bad they are. It might be just a pulled muscle or a bone injury which needs surgery.
不要选 A（诊断简单），原文说有时只有专家能分辨差异（Only an expert can tell...），说明诊断并不容易。
John 指出脚后跟受伤的严重程度差异巨大（vary enormously in how bad they are），对应选项“有些比其他的更严重”。

options.option: use a source written by their professor.
options.optionContent: use a source written by their professor.

questions.question: On the subject of causes of heel injuries, the students agree to

analyses.content: They're all relevant, but for simplicity let's just pick one cause.
不要选 C，教授只是推荐了那本包含研究的杂志，并不是教授自己写的（written by their professor）。
虽然有很多原因，但为了简单起见，两人决定只挑选一个原因（pick one cause）来讲，即关注单一理由。

options.option: It is commonly confused with balance exercises.
options.optionContent: It is commonly confused with balance exercises.

options.optionContent: It is the least effective part of treatment.

questions.question: What does Cath say about stretching as a treatment?

analyses.content: Cath 强调拉伸需要小心管理，否则可能会造成弊大于利（more harm than good），这意味着它有潜在风险。
Otherwise, you could do yourself more harm than good.
不要选 B，原文说拉伸应该与平衡练习“结合”（combined），而不是被“混淆”（confused）。

questions.question: Which TWO treatment techniques did the female runner find useful for her swollen heel?

analyses.content: Initially, she rested the injury. This did help to reduce the swelling...
注意听态度评价词，虽然还是一点不舒服，但总体评价是 "did help"。
对于这位女性跑者，最初的休息（rested）确实有助于减轻肿胀（did help to reduce the swelling），是有效的。

questions.question: Which TWO treatment techniques did the female runner find useful for her swollen heel?

analyses.content: ...she was shown how to use deep tissue massage techniques, and was surprised at how much freedom of movement this created...
不要选 E（冰敷）、B（超声波）或 D（平衡练习），原文分别用 "wasn't helping"（没用）和 "unconvinced about its value"（不信服）否定了它们。
深层组织按摩（massage）让她惊讶于脚部恢复了很大的活动自由度，证明非常有效。

questions.question: Which TWO sports did the male sprinter find most effective during his rehabilitation programme?

analyses.content: And if he used light weights, he could train without pain.
不要选 A（游泳），原文说踢腿动作实际上加重了伤情（aggravating the injury）。
男性短跑运动员发现使用轻重量进行举重训练（use weights）时，可以无痛训练（train without pain），是有效的。

questions.question: Which TWO sports did the male sprinter find most effective during his rehabilitation programme?

analyses.content: He also tried cycling, and found this beneficial, as his foot was not making contact with the ground.
不要选 C（草地跑）或 E（跳跃），原文提到这两项运动后脚后跟都会酸痛（sore afterwards）。
他尝试骑行（cycling），发现这很有益（beneficial），因为脚不着地。
